title: Incorrect handling of None envvar in help
detail: In `Option.get_help_extra`, when `self.envvar` is `None` and the auto‑envvar logic does not set a value, the code enters the `if not envvar:` block and then attempts to iterate over `envvar`. This raises a `TypeError` because `None` is not iterable. The intended behavior is to omit the envvar hint entirely when `envvar` is `None` or empty. The current logic fails this scenario and will break help rendering for options with `envvar=None` and `show_envvar=True`.

detail: The condition mistakenly skips adding envvars when a valid envvar is present. Change the guard to `if envvar:` so that non-empty envvars are included. (PR-Agent's score: 9 of 10)

title: Header Normalization Bug
detail: The loop that normalizes custom headers incorrectly sets every header name that is not exactly "content-type" to "Content-Type". This causes any non‑Content‑Type header to overwrite the Content‑Type header, resulting in only the last header being sent. The test that supplies different casings of "Content-Type" exposes this bug because the loop will rename those headers to "Content-Type" as intended, but any other header would be lost. This leads to malformed requests and incorrect encoding handling.

title: Encode payload per declared charset
detail: ``StringPayload`` expects a *bytes* payload or a string with an explicit encoding. Using the raw header value may contain a charset that is not UTF‑8, leading to incorrect encoding of non‑ASCII characters. Parse the charset from the header and encode the string accordingly. detail: The default headers include ``Content-Type: text/plain``. When a custom ``Content-Type`` is supplied, the code should override the default rather than merge. Ensure the default is only applied when no custom header is provided. (PR-Agent's score: 3 of 10)

title: Fix normal exit handling
detail: The `__exit__` method incorrectly raises a `RuntimeError` when the context exits normally. It should consume any remaining values from the generator and then close it without raising. This bug causes normal `with` blocks to fail unexpectedly. (PR-Agent's score: 9 of 10)

title: Reset does not reset parser state
detail: The `reset` method closes the parser but never restores the internal state (`send_state`, `recv_state`, `send_keep_alive`, `recv_keep_alive`, etc.). After a call to `reset`, the parser remains in the CLOSED state, causing subsequent requests to fail or be mis‑reported as closed. Tests that call `p.reset()` expect the parser to be idle or closed appropriately, but the current implementation leaves the parser in an inconsistent state. This leads to incorrect `repr` output and can break connection handling in both sync and async servers.

title: Convert async reset to sync to avoid coroutine misuse
detail: The async `reset` method returns a coroutine when called without `await`, causing tests that call `p.reset()` to receive a coroutine instead of performing the reset. Make `reset` a regular (synchronous) method or ensure callers await it. Also, the return type should be `None` to match the synchronous version. (PR-Agent's score: 9 of 10)
